title: Constraints and Defaults
subtitle: NOT NULL, UNIQUE, CHECK, DEFAULT, and generated columns
author: KERNAL Team

whyItExists.problem: Application code is fallible — bugs, race conditions, or direct database access can insert invalid data. Constraints enforce data rules at the database level, regardless of how data is inserted.
whyItExists.solution: Constraints and defaults ensure data validity without relying solely on application logic.
whyItExists.whenToUse: Whenever a business rule can be expressed as a constraint, put it in the database too — defense in depth.
whyItExists.whenNotToUse: Very complex validation logic (ML model outputs, cross-system rules) belongs in application code. Constraints shine for simple invariants: not null, valid range, unique, valid enum value.

content.code:
CREATE TABLE products (
  id          BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
  sku         TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,              -- no nulls, no duplicates
  name        TEXT NOT NULL,
  price       NUMERIC(10,2) NOT NULL,
  quantity    INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  discount    NUMERIC(5,2) DEFAULT 0
    CHECK (discount >= 0 AND discount <= 100),  -- inline CHECK
  category    TEXT NOT NULL
    CHECK (category IN ('electronics', 'clothing', 'food', 'other')),
  weight_kg   NUMERIC(8,2)
    CHECK (weight_kg > 0),
  created_at  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);

-- Named constraint (appears in error messages)
ALTER TABLE products
  ADD CONSTRAINT chk_price_positive CHECK (price > 0);

-- Multi-column UNIQUE constraint
ALTER TABLE team_memberships
  ADD CONSTRAINT uq_team_user UNIQUE (team_id, user_id);

CREATE TABLE orders (
  id            BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
  quantity      INTEGER NOT NULL,
  unit_price    NUMERIC(10,2) NOT NULL,
  -- Automatically computed, stored on disk
  total_price   NUMERIC(10,2) GENERATED ALWAYS AS (quantity * unit_price) STORED,
  created_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);

-- You cannot INSERT into a generated column
INSERT INTO orders (quantity, unit_price) VALUES (3, 29.99);
-- total_price is automatically 89.97
SELECT total_price FROM orders WHERE id = 1;  -- 89.97

content.text: Give constraints meaningful names. An unnamed CHECK constraint shows as 'orders_price_check' in errors — a named one shows as 'chk_positive_price', making error messages self-documenting.

questions.question: You want to ensure 'email' is unique per user per organization. Which constraint?
questions.explanation: A multi-column UNIQUE constraint (org_id, email) ensures the combination is unique — the same email can appear in different organizations, but not twice within the same organization. UNIQUE on email alone would prevent the same email across all organizations.

faq.q: Can CHECK constraints reference other tables?
faq.a: No — CHECK constraints can only reference columns within the same row. For cross-table validation, use triggers or application code. Example: CHECK that an order's total equals the sum of its line items requires a trigger, not a CHECK constraint.

examples: E-commerce: CHECK (price > 0), CHECK (quantity >= 0) prevent negative prices and stock counts at the DB level
SaaS: UNIQUE (organization_id, email) ensures unique emails per organization, allowing the same email in different orgs
